label: GO after a2 S2 rewarded, largest when that reward followed a loss (esp. at S1)
terms: ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * (tv("prev_reward", -1) == 0) ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * (prev_state == -1) ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * ep_dec ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * np.clip(-choice, 0, None) ;; ((phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & isin(prev_state, [2, -1]) & isin(prev_action, [2, -1])) * (tv("prev_reward", -1) == 0) * (tv("prev_reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase != GO)
explanation: Fires only at GO; D1/D2 are zero. Magnitude is driven by the last trial being a2 -> S2 rewarded (common rewarded a2; or window-first trial with a reward shown). Within that, the key is reward novelty: activation is large when the trial before was unrewarded (+0.42), extra large when that loss was at S1 (+0.35), and reduced when there was an earlier reward before that loss (-0.23); after two consecutive rewards it is near zero. Grows with the strength of the a2 policy logit (-choice) and fades across the episode (ep_dec). All other last-trial patterns give ~0. Only observed cues plus the model policy logit; no future variables. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.65 (dev 0.66), above the additive all ceiling 0.41 because the terms are interactions; the (phase != GO) term is just an offset correction.

issues: The explanation says the a2 policy logit has a 'small weight'. That understates it badly. The policy is a large driver with a strongly nonlinear shape. Replacing B*np.clip(-choice,0,None) with B*np.exp(-choice) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.647 to 0.735. Intermediate shapes rise steadily: clip^2 0.668, clip^3 0.684, clip^4 0.697. B*np.exp(-choice) plus the phase offset alone reaches 0.49, about the same as B + 'loss before' (0.50). The linear term was also not small in effect: dropping it costs 0.065 (0.647 -> 0.582).

In the exp(-choice) fit the reward-history weights shrink. The fresh-reward term (L1) goes from +0.42 to +0.36, the 'loss at S1' term (L2) from +0.35 to +0.17, and the 'reward before the loss' term (R) from -0.23 to -0.17. So the label's 'largest when the loss was at S1' is partly carried by policy strength. The S1 effect is still real: dropping L2 costs 0.04 on test.

There is one systematic error class in misses: the window's first slot (prev_state == -1, reward shown, actual about 1.1-1.5). Every worst-fit window is of this type, with predictions of only 0.2-0.4. The explanation says that on the first trial activation needs 'simply a reward being shown'. In fact first-slot activations are bimodal, near 0 or about 1.4, depending on history the window does not contain. Policy-shaped first-slot terms only partly fix this: the FS*choice variants did not beat the plain exp(-choice) model.

Claims that check out: the feature fires only at GO. It needs the last trial to be a2 -> S2 rewarded; the residuals after a2 S1 r and after all a1 patterns are about -0.06. The fresh-reward-after-loss term is the main effect (B alone 0.18; B + L1 0.50). The 'reward before that loss' term and ep_dec each add about 0.02-0.035 on test. The (phase != GO) term adds about 0.047 on test, which matches the stated 0.60 without it. It only re-fits the non-B GO level to about 0. No future variables are used. Note that 'action' at GO is future, so I did not use the B*(action==2) gain (+0.026).
